title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §1 'Courbes standard' of the notes 'Structure à l'infini des M_{g,ν}'. On the previous page a standard curve over an algebraically closed field k is defined as a quasi-projective k-scheme X, each of whose irreducible components has dimension 1, and whose only singularities are ordinary double points (nodes), étale-locally isomorphic to xy=0. It has a canonical completion X̂, a projective curve, with I = X̂∖X a finite set of smooth points (the 'points at infinity') and A the finite set of nodes.

This page states that giving X is equivalent to giving the pair (X̂, I). Here X̂ is a projective nodal curve and I is a finite reduced (étale) subscheme of the smooth locus, i.e. a finite subset of X̂^lisse(k).

Let Y = (X̂)~ be the normalization of X̂. It coincides with the smooth completion of the normalization X̃ of X; the notation X̂̃ = X̃̂ records this.
- The preimage Ĩ of I satisfies Ĩ = Y∖X̃, and Ĩ → I is a bijection (2), because the points of I are smooth. Grothendieck therefore identifies smooth points of X̂ with their preimages in Y.
- The preimage Ã of the node set A gives a map Ã → A of degree 2 (3), since each node has exactly two branches. This yields a fixed-point-free involution σ_Ã on Ã.

The next page completes the dictionary. Standard curves, up to isomorphism, correspond to data consisting of:
- a smooth projective curve Y, possibly disconnected;
- disjoint finite subsets Ã and I of Y(k);
- a fixed-point-free involution σ on Ã.

The inverse construction pinches Y∖I along the involution: X is the universal scheme receiving Y∖I in which the points of each σ-orbit are identified. X̂ is recovered by the same pinching applied to Y.

This is the standard 'normalization plus gluing data' description of nodal (pointed) curves. It sets up the combinatorial description of the boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}: components of Y give vertices, σ-orbits give edges, and I gives legs. That is the dual-graph or modular-graph stratification.
errors: The equivalence holds only for the groupoids of isomorphisms, as the next page says. General morphisms of curves do not correspond to morphisms of gluing data.

The existence of the pinched quotient as a scheme (universal in (Sch)) is asserted without proof. It is fine here because a finite set of points lies in an affine open of a quasi-projective curve; in general it is Ferrand's pinching theorem.
Neither connectedness of X nor a stability condition is imposed at this stage, so Y may be disconnected and may have rational components with few special points.

ideas.what: A nodal curve with marked smooth points at infinity is equivalent to its completion plus a finite set of smooth points.
ideas.modern_name: Open curve versus pointed compact nodal curve (X̂, I)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA 1 Exp. XIII (tame fundamental group of open curves); the M_{g,ν} viewpoint is in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: A nodal curve is encoded by its normalization, the preimage of the nodes, and a fixed-point-free involution on that preimage; the curve is recovered by pinching.
ideas.modern_name: Normalization and clutching/gluing data; dual (modular) graph of a stable curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Serre, Groupes algébriques et corps de classes, for singular curves); Deligne–Mumford, Knudsen clutching morphisms; Ferrand 2003 for general pinching
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the boundary structure of M̄_{g,ν} in this spirit, but without this explicit dictionary

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine foundational set-up (normalization and gluing data for nodal curves), well known and standard in Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen. Its only interest is as the opening of Grothendieck's own treatment of the boundary of M_{g,ν}.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Soit X̂̃ = X̂̃ la normalisée de X̂': in the image the two symbols appear to stack the hat and tilde in opposite orders (tilde over hat = hat over tilde). This expresses that the normalization of the completion equals the completion of the normalization, rather than a trivial identity.
'Ĩ = X̂̃ ∖ X̃': the I carries an overwritten correction in the manuscript.
'l'un des [-ses-] "points à l'infini"' is probably 'l'ens. des "points à l'infini" de X̃' (the set of points at infinity), not 'l'un des'.
'ou ce qui revient au =' should read 'ou ce qui revient au même'.
